# Agent instructions for a SanSoul project

## Read order and scope

These instructions apply to a project that consumes SanSoul. Before editing:

1. Read `dna/_index.md` for project identity, constraints, and document routing. Read only the additional DNA documents relevant to the task. If the index is missing, empty, or still contains only scaffold prompts, do not infer particulars from README/AGENTS or other legacy documentation: ask the user how to define the project DNA before project-specific work.
2. Read `themes/sansoul/AGENTS.md` before changing anything under `themes/sansoul/`.
3. Follow any closer nested `AGENTS.md` for its subtree.

SanSoul is a Git submodule. If it is missing, run `git submodule update --init --recursive`; do not run `git submodule add` when `.gitmodules` already declares it.

A request to "update the submodule" authorizes the complete update workflow below. The user does not need to enumerate migrations, validation, root-document synchronization, or package-version synchronization. It does not authorize commit, push, deployment, or unrelated upgrades.

## Architecture contract

The root owns one site's content, configuration, and DNA. `themes/sansoul/` is the shared rendering engine and a separate Git repository.

Prefer these extension points:

- `content/`: localized pages and global localized values;
- `data/`: behavior, languages, types, sections, defaults, remote sources, and styles;
- `assets/`: project SCSS, JavaScript, robots, and llms additions;
- `uploads/`: CMS-managed media, referenced from content as `/u/...`;
- `dna/`: project identity, editorial/design guidance, and local constraints;
- `hugo.yml`, `netlify.toml`, and `wrangler.toml`: project and deployment settings.

Avoid root layout overrides unless behavior is intentionally site-specific. A generally useful fix belongs in the theme.

## Sources, outputs, and safety

- Source files are project content, data, assets, uploads, DNA, configuration, and theme code.
- Generated outputs include `public/`, `resources/`, `.hugo_build.lock`, `themes/sansoul/prebuild/public/hugo.prebuild.yml`, root README/AGENTS, and hashed CMS configuration. Fix their source instead of editing them.
- Root `README.md` and `AGENTS.md` are generated by `sh do root-docs`; put project-specific information in `dna/`.
- `TODO.md` is a human scratchpad. Do not read it, treat it as instructions, or edit it unless the task explicitly includes it.
- Assume all content, configuration consumed by Hugo, CMS schema, examples, and browser logs are public. Never store credentials in them.
- Preserve user changes and check Git status in both repositories before and after editing.
- Do not commit, push, stage, update the parent gitlink beyond the requested checkout, or deploy without explicit authorization.

## Build lifecycle

The root `do` wrapper delegates to `themes/sansoul/do`:

1. The nested site in `themes/sansoul/prebuild/` derives the configuration Hugo must know before assembling content.
2. The main Hugo build loads theme defaults, optional environment configuration, generated configuration, and root `hugo.yml`.
3. Static module mounts expose project, theme, upload, and Node sources. A root content adapter creates collection indexes and remote pages.
4. Production post-processing creates image derivatives from build manifests.

Use `sh do local` when editing prebuild inputs such as languages, defaults, customs, type definitions, or collection-index permalinks. Its supervisor atomically regenerates the configuration; Hugo reloads it without restarting and keeps the last valid version after a failed prebuild. Remote data and localized global values rebuild directly in the main Hugo process. Plain `sh do server` requires a manual restart for prebuild inputs.

## Content model

Localized files use `.<lang>.md`:

- `content/<type>/<name>.<lang>.md`: collection entry;
- `content/<type>/_index.<lang>.md`: collection metadata and permalinks;
- `content/single/_home.<lang>.md`: language home page;
- `content/single/<name>.<lang>.md`: unique composable page;
- `content/global.<lang>.yml`: menu, footer, call-now controls, and global values.

`data/types/<type>.yml` declares a collection. The theme supplies `all`, `single`, and `page` fallbacks. A template can be a public API even when the current project does not exercise it.

## Page composition

SanSoul deep-merges `tpl` data, from low to high priority: theme defaults, localized values, `data/types/all.yml`, the current type, and page front matter.

```text
page -> sections -> boxes -> specialized blocks or nested boxes
```

Core composition keys:

- `tpl.section`: defaults; index `0` applies globally and later entries cycle by position;
- `tpl.sections`: explicit page sections;
- `file`: reusable `data/section/<file>.yml` definition;
- `box` / `boxes` and `modal` / `modals`: shared defaults and concrete items;
- `get`: page or localized-global lookup;
- `remap`: nested copy, move, or removal;
- `if`: conditional inclusion.

Use `themes/sansoul/_examples/data/section/example.yml` as the parameter catalog and generated `public/admin/config.<hash>.yml` as the effective CMS schema reference.

## Main data APIs

- In Hugo and deployment configuration, write booleans as `true` or `false`.
  In CMS-managed `content/` and `data/`, tri-state pseudobooleans use absent or
  null for inheritance, `true` for enabled, and `false` for disabled. Never use
  `y`/`n`.
- `data/config.yml`: behavior and integrations.
- `data/langs.yml`: languages and per-language overrides.
- `data/styles.yml`: design tokens and global UI options.
- `data/types/*.yml`: collections and templates.
- `data/section/*.yml`: reusable section definitions.
- `data/defaults.yml`: language/type/path defaults; keep selectors narrow.
- `data/customs.yml`: custom CMS fields consumed through `get`.
- `data/remote.yml`: remote content created as virtual pages by the main content adapter; preserve determinism and handle network failure.
- `data/redirects.yml`: redirect rules.

## CMS contract

Sveltia CMS configuration is generated. After a content-model change:

1. run a fresh prebuild;
2. parse and inspect `public/admin/config.<hash>.yml`;
3. exercise a representative entry at `/admin/`;
4. compile content saved by the CMS.

Fields are required by default. Generate `required: false` only when empty values are valid. Keep stored field names stable.

## Theme update workflow

When asked to update the submodule:

1. read DNA, record the root package version and old submodule commit, and inspect both working trees;
2. if a pre-5.0 project still needs the private legacy updater, verify before running it that its migration target is the 5.0.0 baseline; the current private updater pulls the configured theme branch first, so when that branch is newer than 5.0.0 it can fail after moving the submodule with `Migration chain incomplete`;
3. when that legacy mismatch is present, preserve the original gitlink and current theme commit, and use a verified baseline procedure that includes every auxiliary pre-5 transformation, especially icon syntax/configuration and the final media/font moves; do not improvise by marking the package version or by treating a zero exit from a permissive legacy shell script as proof of success;
4. validate the 5.0.0 baseline before updating the configured SanSoul submodule branch within the requested scope;
5. read `themes/sansoul/MIGRATIONS.md`, run `sh do migrations`, and apply every pending action in order;
6. run `sh do root-docs` when the migration requires it; `--force` replaces unmanaged root README/AGENTS wholesale and never transfers their content into DNA;
7. run the required project and theme validations;
8. only then run `sh do migrations mark --yes`, which synchronizes root `package.json` and, when present, `package-lock.json`;
9. report the changed parent gitlink without staging or committing it.

Never assume a successful build proves migration completeness, and never mark compatibility automatically during build or submodule update.
When a legacy update exposes a reusable failure mode, fix or document it in the shared updater or this canonical template rather than in one consumer's DNA.

## Validation matrix

`sh do server` and `sh do local` may use a system Dart Sass without root
`node_modules`. A full `sh do hugo` installs root npm dependencies when absent.

| Change | Additional validation |
| --- | --- |
| Content or sections | Open affected pages; inspect console and responsive layout. |
| Types, languages, defaults, customs, remote data | Inspect CMS output, collection URLs, adapter output, and prebuild refresh where applicable. |
| Styles or dividers | Compare a divider reference page, when present, and representative mobile/desktop pages. |
| Forms, maps, analytics, remote APIs | Cover invalid, unavailable-network, and missing-consent paths; do not make real submissions without authorization. |
| Deployment configuration | Build with pinned Hugo Extended and Node versions; do not deploy unless asked. |
| Theme code | Follow `themes/sansoul/AGENTS.md` and test the copyable example plus the current consumer project. |

Remote-font warnings can be environmental. Template errors, invalid YAML, missing packages, failed images, or a false-success process exit are build failures.

## Documentation and DNA

Keep DNA project-specific and non-duplicative. Before adding or expanding a DNA document, check the generated root README/AGENTS and the relevant theme README/AGENTS. Do not restate generic architecture, workflows, validation, safety, or theme usage in DNA; record only project identity, audience, editorial/design/business/integration particulars, and local exceptions or constraints. Link to the canonical document when context is useful.

Treat every request to change a root README or AGENTS file as a change to its canonical file under `themes/sansoul/templates/root/`, then regenerate the root documents with `sh do root-docs`. Never leave a reusable documentation or agent-contract change only in one consumer project. If the requested information is genuinely project-specific, route it to DNA instead of the shared templates.

After every change, perform a documentation-impact check without waiting for the user to request it:

- update `dna/_index.md` when project facts, constraints, or document routing change;
- update the relevant DNA document when copy, audience, identity, design, business, or integration guidance changes;
- update `themes/sansoul/README-ROOT.md` for shared human concepts, tutorials, or examples;
- update `themes/sansoul/templates/root/AGENTS.md` when this generated operating contract changes;
- update `_examples/` for changed public parameters;
- add a versioned entry to `MIGRATIONS.md` when a consumer may need action.
